turns.t: Doctor, hello. Sorry, it is my son Arjun, he is limping, I think, since a few days.
Hello Arjun, hello Mrs Menon. Arjun, you're seven, is that right? ~
Seven and a half. ~
Seven and a half. Arjun, when did your leg start to hurt?
Yesterday. One day.
No, no, beta. It is three days, since Saturday. You told me on Saturday evening.
So Arjun says one day, and Mum says three days. I'll write down one to three days for now. Arjun, where does it hurt?
Here. My knee. And this side.
Does it hurt when you stand on it, or all the time?
When I walk. Not when I sit.
Did you fall, or hurt it playing football or at school?
No, he didn't say anything about a fall. The teacher didn't tell us either.
Has he had any fever, been feeling hot or unwell?
No fever, no. He's eating, he's playing, only he walks funny.
Does Arjun take any medicines?
The montelukast for his asthma, 5 mg at night, every day. And I gave ibuprofen, 5 ml, only last night when he was crying.
Right. And what other health problems has he had?
Asthma since he was three, and eczema, on the elbows.
Does he have any allergies?
Peanuts. He gets hives and his lips swell.
Thank you, that's very important. Arjun, I'm going to look at how you walk. Can you walk to the door and back? ~
Okay.
He's limping on the right side, he spends less time on the right leg, and the hip moves fully in all directions, with no pain when I move it.
Is it his hip? ~
The hip moves well, which is reassuring. The knee isn't swollen and isn't hot. I can't see a clear cause today, and I don't want to put a name on it yet. ~
What should we do? ~
Rest from sports for a few days, and let him walk as he feels able. You can give the ibuprofen if he's sore, with food.
He loves football, he will complain. ~
A few days off won't hurt him. Is he sleeping well, is the pain waking him? ~
No, he sleeps through. ~
Good. I'd like to see him again in three days, to check how he's walking.
Three days, fine. And if it gets worse? ~
If he gets a fever, can't put weight on the leg at all, or the knee swells up, bring him straight in.
I will. Thank you, doctor. ~
Bye, doctor. ~

physical_examination.normalized_finding: Right-sided antalgic gait with full hip movement

clinical_uncertainties.description: Child says the limp began one day ago; his mother says three days; summarised as one to three days, not confirmed.

clinical_actions.description: Rest from sports for a few days; ibuprofen with food if sore
Safety-net: bring back if fever, cannot weight bear or knee swells

contradictions_detected: Duration of limp: patient one day vs family member three days (approximate range only).
